title: Traffic safety client abstractions for gradual model rollouts
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: Build an opinionated API + SDK client helpers that let product teams perform canary/A-B/shadow rollouts with predictable safety properties. The goal is to provide transactional primitives for traffic routing, idempotent change operations, and fine-grained permission checks so platform teams can run progressive experiments without manual orchestration. This ticket scopes the PM requirements, acceptance criteria, and integration concerns for engineering and SDK owners.
background: Multiple product teams reported inconsistent behavior when doing canaries: duplicated traffic assignments after retries, difficulty correlating rollout events to audit logs, and unclear permissions for who can escalate a canary to GA. Existing rollout SDK helpers are fragmented between Console UI and server-side orchestration; we need a lightweight client library that is backwards compatible and makes safe defaults easy.
acceptance_criteria: API: Add /rollouts/sessions endpoint that creates a rollout session with a stable session_id and a precondition token for transactional changes
SDK: Provide client helper functions for startSession(), applyTrafficSplit(session_id, traffic_map, precondition_token), shadowTraffic(config) and commitSession()/abortSession()
Idempotency: All mutate endpoints accept an idempotency_key and return a canonical operation_id. Replays with same idempotency_key must be no-op and return the same operation_id
Permissions: Map existing RBAC roles to three new actions: rollouts.create, rollouts.modify, rollouts.commit. Console must enforce mappings and SDK must surface permission errors clearly
Observable: Rollout sessions generate structured telemetry events with session_id and operation_id that appear in Console timelines and Grafana dashboards
Auto-rollback: Provide config hook to attach simple health monitors (latency, error-rate) and automatic abort on configured thresholds; implement prototype for latency regression rule
Backward compatibility: Existing users calling the older /traffic endpoints continue to work and are translated to a session with a single commit if used through SDK shims
notes: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with Eng, SDK and Security. Agreed on leaving storage of session state in control-plane to preserve consistency across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
2026-02-28: Eng suggested optimistic concurrency using precondition tokens (compare-and-swap) to avoid global locks. PM accepted after reviewing race scenarios.
2026-03-02: Security review requested for audit logging and KMS access for session secrets. Security flagged that session precondition tokens must be short-lived and rotatable.
2026-03-04: SDK owners propose default idempotency time window of 24h for rollouts operations, configurable by enterprise tenants. Need final approval from Privacy/Compliance for retention.
2026-03-06: Design feedback: Console should render session timeline with diff view of traffic allocation and highlight shadowed routes. Design to share mocks next week.
2026-03-10: Engineering PR draft created: gh/redwood/rollout-api#412. Early tests for idempotency keys pass in unit tests; integration flaky against dedicated simulator (investigating).
implementation_notes: Prefer session-based semantics rather than ad-hoc traffic patch endpoints to make auditability and rollback simpler
Use precondition_token = sha256(session_id || etag) short-lived; store minimal session metadata in control plane and persist audit events to the event store
Idempotency: server returns operation_id and canonical response on duplicate idempotency_key; SDK will surface convenient wrappers to generate collision-resistant keys
Permission mapping: add three new granular IAM actions and update role templates for Dedicated and Private deployments
Auto-rollback prototype should be controlled by a tenant-level feature flag and not enabled by default
open_questions: What is the default rollback policy for combined velocity + quality regressions?
Should shadow traffic be billed the same as production traffic for hosted customers? Finance input needed
How long should idempotency keys be valid for cross-region retries?
Do we provide a CLI and Terraform provider for rollout sessions or start with SDKs only?
